title: Forenames and Surnames
summary: Headings for individual forenames and surnames, used for works on the etymology of names, are topical headings in the most common form of the name with the qualifier (Name), e.g. Elizabeth (Name). Similar names with different meanings or ethnic backgrounds are separate headings; UFs are alternate spellings only (not nicknames or diminutives); BT is Names, Personal.
validation_rules: For works on the etymology of a forename or surname, the name is a topical heading (150/650) in its most common form with the qualifier `(Name)`, e.g. `Elizabeth (Name)`; `MacCarthy (Name)`. (H 1629.5 sec. 1)
Similar-sounding names with different meanings and similar names from different ethnic backgrounds are separate headings, e.g. `Marii︠a︡ (Name)` and `Mary (Name)`. (H 1629.5 sec. 1)
For inflected foreign-language names, prefer the singular nominative form for forenames and the masculine, singular, nominative form for surnames. (H 1629.5 sec. 1)
UF references are made from alternate spellings, each qualified `(Name)`, e.g. `Ann (Name)` UF `Anne (Name)`. (H 1629.5 sec. 2)
Do not make UF references from nicknames or diminutives; establish them as separate headings if needed, e.g. `Jack (Name)` and `John (Name)` [not `John (Name)` UF `Jack (Name)`]. (H 1629.5 sec. 2)
The broader term is `Names, Personal`. (H 1629.5 sec. 3)

Existing headings with UFs for nicknames, diminutives, or similar names from different ethnic backgrounds remain in use; such UFs are removed and established separately only as required for new cataloging. (H 1629.5 sec. 4)

sections.heading: Background
sections.text: Headings for forenames (a.k.a. given names) and surnames in LCSH are assigned to works about the etymology of names. This instruction sheet provides guidelines for establishing headings for forenames and surnames.

sections.heading: 1. General rule
sections.text:
For works about the etymology of a forename or surname, establish the name as a topical heading. Use the most common form of the name as the heading, and qualify it with the term "name." Examples:

```
150 $a Elizabeth (Name)
150 $a MacCarthy (Name)
```

Establish similar-sounding names with different meanings and similar names from different ethnic backgrounds as separate names. Examples:

```
150 $a Marii︠a︡ (Name)
150 $a Mary (Name)
```

For names in foreign languages that appear in inflected forms, generally prefer the singular nominative form for forenames and the masculine, singular, nominative form for surnames.

sections.heading: 2. UF references
sections.text:
Make UF references from alternate spellings of the name. Qualify each reference with the term "name." Do not make UF references from nicknames or diminutive forms of the name. If required for the work being cataloged, establish a separate heading for the nickname or diminutive form. Examples:

```
150 $a Ann (Name)
450 $a Anne (Name)
```

```
150 $a Jack (Name)
```

```
150 $a John (Name)
[not 450 $a Jack (Name)]
```

sections.heading: 3. BT references
sections.text: Provide the BT reference Names, Personal.

sections.heading: 4. Existing headings
sections.text: Some existing headings contain UF references for nicknames, diminutives, and/or similar names from different ethnic backgrounds. Continue to use the headings. Remove such UFs and establish them as separate headings only as required for new cataloging.
